From 14533a5a6c12e8d7de79d309d4085bf186058fe1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Michael Kao <michael.kao@mediatek.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2020 20:15:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] thermal/drivers/mediatek: Fix bank number settings on mt8183

MT8183_NUM_ZONES should be set to 1
because MT8183 doesn't have multiple banks.

Fixes: a4ffe6b52d27 ("thermal: mediatek: add support for MT8183")
Signed-off-by: Michael Kao <michael.kao@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yi Wang <hsinyi@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Lezcano <daniel.lezcano@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200323121537.22697-6-michael.kao@mediatek.com

diff --git a/drivers/thermal/mtk_thermal.c b/drivers/thermal/mtk_thermal.c
index 76e30603d4d5..6b7ef1993d7e 100644
--- a/drivers/thermal/mtk_thermal.c
+++ b/drivers/thermal/mtk_thermal.c
@@ -211,6 +211,9 @@ enum {
 /* The total number of temperature sensors in the MT8183 */
 #define MT8183_NUM_SENSORS	6
 
+/* The number of banks in the MT8183 */
+#define MT8183_NUM_ZONES               1
+
 /* The number of sensing points per bank */
 #define MT8183_NUM_SENSORS_PER_ZONE	 6
 
@@ -497,7 +500,7 @@ static const struct mtk_thermal_data mt7622_thermal_data = {
  */
 static const struct mtk_thermal_data mt8183_thermal_data = {
 	.auxadc_channel = MT8183_TEMP_AUXADC_CHANNEL,
-	.num_banks = MT8183_NUM_SENSORS_PER_ZONE,
+	.num_banks = MT8183_NUM_ZONES,
 	.num_sensors = MT8183_NUM_SENSORS,
 	.vts_index = mt8183_vts_index,
 	.cali_val = MT8183_CALIBRATION,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/thermal/mtk_thermal.c`**
   - Added a new definition for the number of zones in the MT8183:
     ```c
     #define MT8183_NUM_ZONES 1
     ```
   - Updated the `mt8183_thermal_data` structure to set the `num_banks` field to `MT8183_NUM_ZONES` instead of `MT8183_NUM_SENSORS_PER_ZONE`:
     ```c
     .num_banks = MT8183_NUM_ZONES,
     ```

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification establishes that the MT8183 chip has only one thermal zone (bank), correcting the previous assumption that it had multiple banks. This change ensures that the thermal management system accurately reflects the hardware capabilities of the MT8183, which is crucial for proper thermal regulation and sensor management. The fix directly addresses a bug introduced in a prior commit, ensuring that the thermal data structure correctly represents the MT8183's architecture.

thermal/drivers/mediatek: Fix bank number settings on mt8183

MT8183_NUM_ZONES should be set to 1
because MT8183 doesn't have multiple banks.

Fixes: a4ffe6b52d27 ("thermal: mediatek: add support for MT8183")

Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yi Wang <hsinyi@chromium.org>

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200323121537.22697-6-michael.kao@mediatek.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by incorrectly setting the number of thermal banks for the MT8183 chip, which was defined as having multiple banks instead of the correct single bank configuration. This misconfiguration could lead to improper thermal management and sensor readings, as the system would expect multiple banks to be present when only one exists.

+/* The number of banks in the MT8183 */
+#define MT8183_NUM_ZONES               1
+
 /* The number of sensing points per bank */
 #define MT8183_NUM_SENSORS_PER_ZONE	 6

```c

.num_banks = MT8183_NUM_SENSORS_PER_ZONE,
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because `MT8183_NUM_ZONES` is incorrectly set to a value that implies multiple thermal banks, while the actual configuration for the MT8183 chip should only have one bank. The line setting `.num_banks` to `MT8183_NUM_SENSORS_PER_ZONE` (which is likely greater than 1) leads to improper thermal management and sensor readings, as the system expects multiple banks to be present.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
.num_banks = MT8183_NUM_ZONES,
```
Reason:
The fix involves changing the `.num_banks` assignment to use `MT8183_NUM_ZONES`, which is correctly defined as 1. This adjustment ensures that the thermal management system accurately reflects the MT8183's single bank configuration, thereby preventing any mismanagement of thermal data and ensuring proper sensor readings.
